name: Establish a boundary baseline and close unintended exposure
description: Define the intended boundary as a reviewed baseline, document the intent behind every broad rule, and remove or restrict exposure that no intent supports — starting with administrative interfaces.
responsible_role: Platform Engineering, with Security Engineering accountable for the baseline

steps.action: Export effective boundary rules across every account, region, and network within the declared system boundary, not only production.
Identify all rules permitting ingress from any source, and separately identify exposed administrative and management interfaces.
For each broad rule, record whether the exposure is intended, and if so why; remove or restrict those with no supporting intent.
Move administrative access behind a bastion, authenticating proxy, or private connectivity, and require additional authentication from outside the boundary.
Express the resulting rule set as code and adopt it as the reviewed baseline.
Assess network paths from adjacent non-production accounts into production and restrict them.
Record the baseline and its documented exceptions in the network security policy.

implementation_considerations: Effective reachability matters more than rule definitions. Overlapping rules and network ACLs mean a permissive-looking rule may deny in practice and vice versa; assess the effective path.
Closing exposure without knowing who uses it causes outages. Log first, observe actual sources, then restrict.
Non-production accounts with paths into production are a frequent blind spot and are usually owned by a different team than the one holding the boundary.
Documenting intent is the cheapest step and the one that most reduces future findings, because it converts an ambiguous export into an assessable one.
typical_duration: Weeks; longer where administrative access must be re-architected behind a bastion.
prerequisites: A current system boundary definition covering all accounts and regions
Ability to observe traffic before restricting rules

verification_method.how: Re-export effective boundary rules across the full boundary and confirm no administrative interface is reachable from any source without a documented intent and compensating restriction, and that every remaining broad rule carries recorded intent.

residual_risk_note: A baseline is a point-in-time statement. Without the drift detection in REM-NETSEC-002 it degrades between reviews and cannot evidence a period.
period_limitation_note: Closing exposure now does not change the boundary configuration during an elapsed period. Where a Type 2 period ran with an exposed interface, that condition existed.
notes: Broad ingress is not a deficiency where it is intended. This remediation is as much about recording intent as about closing rules.
